description:
PROBLEM: each dsqgen call copies the 123-file template tree into a temp directory and deletes it (benchbox TPC-DS c_tools.py around line 296); on a quiet machine that is 27 of 33 ms per call, dsqgen itself about 5 ms. Tests call it hundreds of times per run.

CHANGE (product code): stage the template tree once per process (or per template set) and write only the edited template per call into a per-call directory, or link unchanged files and replace the edited one; generate_with_parameters rewrites a template inside the work directory, so a linked file must be replaced, never written through.

DECISION GATES:
G1 Output identity: for all 99 queries and several seeds/streams, generated SQL is byte-identical before and after (local script, results in PR body); the TPC-DS answer/qualification tests pass.
G2 Safety: show the source template tree is never modified (checksum before/after a full run), including under concurrent calls from xdist workers.
G3 Windows: symlinks may be unavailable; use copy for the edited file and hard links or a once-per-process copy for the rest, and keep the Windows CI job green.
G4 Measure per-call time and the TPC-DS tests' CI times; keep the change only if it is faster.
G5 Show each dsqgen call edits exactly one template (the small-scale template overrides touch only one file); if more, write each edited file per call.
G6 Fall back to copying on OSError (hard links fail across devices, EXDEV). G2's concurrency check must also cover threads (the concurrent bound-queries test).
